messages:
maria: heads-up — after last night's runtime upgrade to v0.9.3 the prefix cache hit-rate dropped ~4x for prod model-rl-7b. seeing ~75% more token generation and higher tail latency. can anyone who touched kernel selection weigh in?
chris: confirmed on our dashboards. prefix_cache.hits 12k -> 3k, misses 2.6k -> 18k in the 00:00-06:00 window. logs show a lot of near-identical prompts missing.
suresh: timeline — we rolled in kernel selector change + new attention opt + per-layer quant profile at 23:30. could be any of those.
maria: attaching quick traces from a repro run:
```
# sample p99 latency change per request-id
req a1: p99 86ms -> 210ms
req b2: p99 90ms -> 220ms
# prefix cache stats (local repro)
prefix_cache.hits 120 -> 28
prefix_cache.misses 30 -> 124
```
olivia: did the cache key format change? I remember we added model_variant metadata to key in v0.9.2 but that was reverted. double-checking key hashing code now.
chris: grep shows keygen is the same, but the hashed input order changed subtly in kernel path because attention cache now stores transposed KV shapes to optimize matmul. that could change serialization order when we were accidentally hashing raw tensors.
maria: oh that matches — we had a workaround before to canonicalize shapes but it relied on old runtime behavior. if the canonicalization is broken, keys will differ across upgrades.
suresh: quick fix idea — stop hashing tensor memory buffer directly. compute deterministic fingerprint from token ids + sequence length + model_version + kernel_build_id. adding kernel_build_id will also make caches incompatible across kernels (but that's safer than silent mismatches).
olivia: agree. short-term mitigation: add kernel_build_id to the key and backfill a flag to allow serving to prefer cached values from previous build for 24h. longer term: fix canonicalization code.
perf-bot: alert: prefix_cache.hit_rate drop detected on model-rl-7b (group: prod). baseline 78% -> 19% after 2026-03-15T23:30Z.
maria: also saw that quantized weights changed a few low-bit layers. hypothesis: quantization tweaks changed hidden representations slightly leading to different next-token logits which invalidates downstream prompt canonicalization that relied on exact float matches.
suresh: we ran a small diff on kv-cache fingerprints (sha1 on canonical repr) across old vs new build. 87% of prefixes are byte-different after kernel+quant bump (most differences in L2 rounding). I'll paste the script we used:
```bash
python -c "
# pseudo
for p in prefixes:
  a = repr_kv(prefix, build_old)
  b = repr_kv(prefix, build_new)
  print(prefix.id, sha1(a), sha1(b))
"
```
chris: interesting — so mismatch is in KV contents not keygen. that explains misses. two mitigation paths: 1) make cache key only depend on tokens and model_version (coarser) and allow KV re-computation when representation differs, or 2) make KV stable across builds (hard).
olivia: option 1 reduces hit-rate but avoids silent wrong-content reuse. we should NOT serve mismatched KV across quant changes. safety first.
maria: agreed. immediate action items:
- revert the kernel selector tweak in canary clusters (deploy-bot initiated?)
- add kernel_build_id to keygen and log prefix fingerprints for 48h
- add warmup job to precompute common prefixes after any build change
chris: I can rollback kernel selector on canary now. starting deploy.
deploy-bot: deploy started to canary (eng-runtime-canary) — rolling back kernel-selector v2 -> v1. ETA 4m.
perf-bot: canary metrics will stream to #perf-dash in ~5m.
suresh: I'll land the keygen change in a small patch and flag it behind a feature gate. that will make cache semantics explicit.
maria: for warmup we should target top-500 prefixes (from logs) per region and fire prewarm jobs after any runtime/model change. that should bring hit-rate back quickly.
olivia: logging improvement: also record a truncated sha1 of KV that can be used to alert when >20% prefixes diverge post-deploy.
chris: quick experiment results — after adding kernel_build_id to keys in a staging run, we saw hit-rate for old-build traffic drop (expected) but no silent incorrect cache reuse. p99 tail latency stable.
maria: plan documented. owners: chris (rollback/canary), suresh (keygen patch + KV fingerprinting), olivia (warmup job + logging), maria (coordinator + customer comms).
olivia: I'll add an eval to the CI that runs a tiny suite: apply runtime build -> compute KV fingerprint delta on top-200 prefixes and fail if >30%.
maria: thanks team. follow-up meeting 10:30 to sync on post-rollback metrics. if anyone finds a faster root cause (e.g., a single layer quant tweak) drop it here. :thumbsup:
